name: Salento and the Cocora Valley
tagline: A colourful coffee town and a valley of towering wax palms in the misty green hills of the UNESCO Coffee Cultural Landscape.
highlight: Walking among the world's tallest palms, rising out of the mist above green pastures.
shortDescription: The heart of Colombia's Coffee Axis, with the pretty village of Salento, the Cocora Valley's 60-metre wax palms, coffee farm tours, hummingbirds and trout.

image.alt: The tall wax palms of the Cocora Valley rising from green meadows

intro: Salento is a small village in the Quindío department, in the coffee-growing heartland of Colombia, and the gateway to the Cocora Valley. The whole region, with its terraced hillsides of coffee, bamboo-and-mud farmhouses and traditions, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: the Coffee Cultural Landscape of Colombia. Salento itself is a delight, with brightly painted single-storey houses and wooden balconies on Calle Real, a shopping street of crafts and cafés.

The main draw is the Cocora Valley, home to the Quindío wax palm, Colombia's national tree, which grows up to 60 metres, the tallest palm in the world. The palms rise above green pastures and cloud forest, with cows grazing at their feet. The classic loop hike takes 5 to 6 hours through forest, across rope bridges and to a hummingbird sanctuary, before emerging among the palms.

Around Salento, coffee farms offer tours where you can see the process from picking to roasting, and taste the results. Filandia, another pretty village, is nearby. The area is best enjoyed over two or three days, with time to slow down.
